overview: The Philippines is an island country in South-East Asia, made up of more than 7,000 islands in the western Pacific. Its capital is Manila, part of the huge Metro Manila area. The Philippines was a Spanish colony for more than 300 years and then an American territory, becoming independent in 1946. Filipino and English are its official languages, and most Filipinos are Christian.

geography.text: The islands fall into three main groups: Luzon in the north, the Visayas in the middle and Mindanao in the south. Most are mountainous and volcanic, with active volcanoes such as Mayon and Taal. The Philippines lies on the Pacific Ring of Fire and in the path of typhoons, and its seas have some of the richest coral reefs in the world.

history.text: Ferdinand Magellan's expedition reached the islands in 1521, and Spain ruled them for more than 300 years, naming them after King Philip II. After the Philippine Revolution of 1896 and the Spanish–American War, the United States took control. The Philippines became independent in 1946, and the 'People Power' revolution of 1986 peacefully removed the dictator Ferdinand Marcos.

events.title: Magellan arrives
events.text: Magellan's expedition reaches the islands; he is killed at Mactan.

events.title: Spanish colony
events.text: Spain begins its colonisation of the islands.

events.title: US rule
events.text: Spain gives the Philippines to the United States.

events.title: People Power
events.text: Peaceful protests end the Marcos dictatorship.

government.text: The Philippines is a presidential republic modelled on the United States. The President is elected for a single six-year term. Congress has a Senate and a House of Representatives.

economy.text: The Philippines has a fast-growing economy built on services, especially call centres and business process outsourcing, and on money sent home by millions of Filipinos working abroad. It also exports electronics, coconut products and bananas.

culture.text: The Philippines has more than 7,000 islands. Its culture blends Malay, Spanish and American influences; it is mostly Catholic, and Filipino and English are official languages. The Banaue rice terraces, carved into mountains 2,000 years ago, are a UNESCO site.

items.title: Banaue rice terraces
items.text: Mountain terraces called the 'eighth wonder of the world'.

items.title: Jeepneys
items.text: Brightly decorated buses that began as US army jeeps.

items.title: Karaoke
items.text: Hugely popular; the Karaoke Sing Along System was patented by a Filipino.

sport.text: Basketball is the national obsession, and the Philippines co-hosted the 2023 Basketball World Cup. Boxer Manny Pacquiao won world titles in eight weight divisions. Gymnast Carlos Yulo won two Olympic golds in 2024.

items.title: Manny Pacquiao
items.text: World champion in eight weight classes.

items.title: Hidilyn Diaz
items.text: Won the Philippines' first Olympic gold, in weightlifting, in 2021.

items.title: Carlos Yulo
items.text: Two gymnastics golds at the 2024 Olympics.

didYouKnow: The Philippines has more than 7,600 islands.
Jeepneys, the colourful buses of Manila, began as US army jeeps left after the Second World War.

keyPeople.text: His novels inspired the fight against Spanish rule.
